Public affairs and ESG · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

ESG questionnaire triage

Nicole · ESG Analyst

An auto parts manufacturer receives 22 ESG questionnaires a year, each with 80 to 250 questions, and about 60% of them repeat across questionnaires with different wording.

When it runs
When a new ESG questionnaire arrives from a customer or rating platform, by email from the buyer or a platform notification, before questions are distributed to internal areas
What it delivers in production
On the first day after receipt, the analyst gets the triage spreadsheet with each question classified, the passage from the source that answers it with the page, and the area that needs to collect the missing data.
Who decides
Classifies and points to sources; the analyst answers
Effort
Calibrate on 3 questionnaires; 4 reviewed real rounds
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# ESG questionnaire triage rules

## Classes
- READY: the knowledge base excerpt answers in full and the required evidence is available.
- PARTIAL: the excerpt covers part of it, or the required evidence is not available.
- NO ANSWER: there is no documented practice. A policy that only states intent ("rejects", "supports") is not a practice.
- NEEDS NEW DATA: the practice is documented, the number is not published.
- Scope 3 never uses scope 1 and 2 data.
- Certification per plant. Any plant expired on the base date or without a certificate: PARTIAL.
- OUTDATED: previous answer whose data year is earlier than the year of the current document in the knowledge base.

## Areas and collection times (by the question's topic)
| topic | Area | Collection time |
|---|---|---|
| emissions | Sustainability | 5 days |
| scope3 | Sustainability with procurement | 45 days |
| verification | Sustainability | 20 days |
| water, energy | Utilities | 3 days |
| suppliers | Procurement | 25 days |
| certification | Quality | 10 days |
| people | HR | 10 days |
| ethics, human_rights | Compliance | 5 days |

## Rules with no leeway
- Days to the deadline in calendar days from the base date. E.g.: from 2026-11-18 to 2026-12-04 is 16 days; Q3 (45), Q4 (20), Q6 (25) and Q7 (25) go past it.
- Percentages over the total number of questions. E.g.: 2 NO ANSWER out of 12 = 16.7%.
- Bands add up. E.g.: 16.7% and Q7 about child labor go to the sustainability manager; 4 questions past the deadline do not reach 6, no extension.
- Employee name, employee ID, phone extension or contact does not appear, not even quoted from the previous answer. E.g.: the previous answer of Q9 goes out with only the number and the date.
- A generic answer from the answer bank does not promote the class. E.g.: "periodic audits" does not make Q6 READY.
- A topic present in another breakdown is PARTIAL, not NO ANSWER. E.g.: Q5 (reused water): p. 41 gives water withdrawn by source and not reuse: PARTIAL, Utilities, 3 days. NO ANSWER stays at 2 of 12 (16.7%).
- The final answer, the run report and the STATE are outputs too: what a rule says to omit does not appear in them, not even to explain the exclusion.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

# Knowledge base excerpts (document, version, page)

- Human_Rights_Policy_2025_v3, p. 2: policy approved by the board in 2025-03; rejects forced labor and child labor in the company and in the supply chain. Does not describe a verification procedure at suppliers. PDF available.
- GHG_Inventory_2025_v1, p. 3: base year 2025, scope 1 = 18,420 tCO2e, scope 2 (location-based) = 9,310 tCO2e. Scope 3 not inventoried. PDF available.
- GHG_Inventory_2025_v1, p. 4: third-party verification contracted in 2026-09; verification statement not yet issued.
- Sustainability_Report_2025_v2, p. 38: 62% of electricity from renewable sources in 2025. PDF available.
- Sustainability_Report_2025_v2, p. 41: water withdrawn by source (well 61%, utility 39%). Does not report reuse.
- Sustainability_Report_2025_v2, p. 55: lost-time injury frequency rate of 1.8 in 2025. PDF available.
- Supplier_Policy_2024_v2, p. 5: annual audit of all critical suppliers. The report does not say how many were done.
- Code_of_Conduct_2025_v4, p. 8: anonymous whistleblowing channel, operated by a third party, 24 hours. Public link available.
- Diversity_Policy_2025_v1, p. 3: target of 30% women in leadership by 2028, with half-yearly tracking. The current number is not published.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent does not write the final answer or fill in the customer's portal; it locates the source and proposes the classification, and the analyst answers. A question with no source in the company comes out as NO ANSWER, never with plausible text built from a generic policy: claiming a nonexistent practice in an ESG questionnaire is a misleading claim. Certification is reported per plant and with its validity, not as a yes for the whole company. Employee data cited in internal reports does not go into the knowledge base.

Common mistakes

  • Answering yes about a policy just because the document exists, without checking approval by senior management, which is what the question assesses.
  • Reusing an old answer with the previous year's emissions figure, which the platform compares with the public report; the discrepancy brings the score down.
  • Marking a scope 3 question as ready using scope 1 and 2 data.
  • Reporting a certification for the whole company when only some of the plants are certified.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Analyst time per questionnaire, from receipt to submissionfrom 3 days to 1 day, with triage on the first dayestimate based on the described routine
Unanswered questions identified on the first day rather than the day before the deadlinefrom close to 0 to 90% or more, measured in calibrationestimate based on the described routine
Answers sent with a traceable source (document and page)from not measured to 100%process target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Triage of Automaker A's supplier sustainability questionnaire, received on 2026-08-28, deadline 2026-09-26, 164 questions.

SUMMARY: 97 with a ready answer (59%), 31 partial (19%), 24 with no answer in the company (15%), 12 require new data (7%).

Q-14 | Do you have a human rights policy approved by senior management? | READY | source: Human Rights Policy v3, p. 2, approved by the board in 2025-03 | previous answer: Automaker C questionnaire, 2026-02, same question | required evidence: policy PDF, available

Q-37 | Scope 3 emissions, purchased goods and services category, in tCO2e | NO ANSWER | the 2025 inventory covers only scopes 1 and 2 | area: sustainability with procurement | effort estimate: collection of 6 to 8 weeks, does not fit the deadline; suggest answering "in progress" with a plan

Q-52 | Percentage of water reused in the process | PARTIAL | 2025 report, p. 41, reports volume withdrawn by source, not reuse | area: utilities | data exists in the metering system, 3-day collection

Q-88 | Audits of critical suppliers carried out during the year | REQUIRES NEW DATA | the supplier policy provides for them, the report does not give a number | area: procurement

Q-121 | Current ISO 14001 certification? | READY | certificate valid until 2027-05-14, plants 1 and 2; plant 3 not certified, state this | evidence: certificate PDF

QUESTIONS WITH A COLLECTION TIME LONGER THAN THE QUESTIONNAIRE DEADLINE: 5 (listed in the Alert tab).
